A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SAM/DISCO research work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: V2 reports original experiments across five datasets in Table 2 and original counterfactual analyses in Section 4.4 and Appendix E.4.

after.justification: V3 reports original experiments across six datasets, corrected sDISCO results, counterfactual analyses, and a new runtime and memory study in Appendix H.5.

M1.justification: V2's sDISCO uses globally weighted centering and normalization. V3 replaces this with an exact factorization computing all local covariances and averaging their correlations (Section 3.2, Appendix G). Appendix B explicitly confirms a corresponding implementation correction. This changes a central estimator; DISCOm and the general regularized prediction objective are retained.

E1.justification: V3 adds MNLI three-way sentence-pair classification with negation-based shortcuts, extending evaluation from vision to language. The original five datasets and both dSprites counterfactual scenarios remain; relocating their descriptions does not constitute new coverage.

E2.justification: IRM and Fishr become evaluated comparators on the retained FairFace and Waterbirds benchmarks and on MNLI (Table 2), using adaptations to target/bias groups. V3 also evaluates naive DISCO in its new runtime comparison. The regression counterfactual comparison drops DISCOm, which appeared alongside sDISCO in v2.

E3.justification: The new MNLI experiment uses TinyBERT and worst-group accuracy for selection and evaluation on biased data. V3 also introduces a controlled runtime protocol across batch sizes 64–1024 and IRM/Fishr search grids. Appendix H.4 revises the counterfactual R² normalization, without establishing whether those experiments were rerun. Existing methods' appendix hyperparameter grids are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix H.5 adds a substantial scalability analysis comparing epoch times and out-of-memory failures across nine methods and four batch sizes, directly testing computational claims previously unsupported by such measurements. The existing counterfactual studies remain, with revisions to the regression comparison rather than an entirely new causal analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report benchmark means ± standard deviations across unspecified runs, without seed lists, confidence intervals, or significance tests. V3 retains this practice for added results. Its timing table reports means and OOM outcomes without introducing an uncertainty estimation procedure; hyperparameter-grid run counts describe configurations.

E6.justification: Table 2 replaces the corrected implementation's sDISCO results: dSprites R² 0.619→0.687, Blob 0.788→0.751, YaleB balanced accuracy 0.694→0.770, FairFace 0.854→0.850, and Waterbirds 0.863→0.874. MNLI, IRM/Fishr, and runtime/OOM results are added. The counterfactual sDISCO row changes from (0.067, 0.6474) to (0.058, 0.7181), exactly v2's DISCOm values; that numerical match is unexplained.

T1.justification: V3 replaces the earlier sDISCO consistency sketch with an exact factorization theorem, derivation, and memory-complexity analysis in Appendix G. DISCOm consistency now requires m to grow rather than permitting fixed m. V3 also corrects the main-text spurious-effect sign to match the appendix and adds an explicit positivity assumption. Renaming the stable pathway alone is not a mathematical change.

C1.justification: The central computational contribution is recast from two new consistent estimators to a subsampled computation and an exact single-shot factorization with quadratic memory. The introduction also qualifies the best-achievable mitigation claim under hidden confounding by excluding valid proxies. The overarching SAM, causal-stability, and competitive debiasing claims remain.

C2.justification: Section 2.2 adds overlap failure conditions, selective treatment of useful mediators, and proxy-based exceptions to hidden-confounder limitations. Section 6 explicitly discusses observed bias-label requirements and distinguishes visually assigned sex labels from gender; the skin-tone/race caveat already existed. Waterbirds background bias is described as mediation instead of collider bias, while its generating equation remains unchanged.

D1.justification: V3 replaces the anonymized code placeholder with a concrete repository address and adds the TinyBERT checkpoint, IRM/Fishr adaptation details and grids, and runtime hardware, preprocessing, workers, and precision. It newly mentions label noise and specifies YaleB's selection vector, without establishing changed experiments. V2's dedicated reproducibility statement describing frameworks and automated configuration files is removed.

R1.justification: New Section 1.1 and Appendix C substantially position the work within discriminative causal representation learning with observed biases. They expand comparisons with Makar, Veitch, and Puli/NURD and add discussion and citations concerning generative learning, latent confounding, causal discovery, and proxies. Wang et al.'s existing V-statistic decomposition receives a more explicit role in defining sDISCO's computational novelty.

P1.justification: The introduction and method narrative undergo substantial explanatory rewriting, including the counterfactually stable-effect terminology and expanded assumptions discussion. Dataset equations move from the main text into Appendix H.1. Appendices are reorganized around corrections, contextualization, proofs, and experiments, and a limitations section replaces the previous reproducibility section.

P2.justification: V3 changes the single-column preprint main text to a two-column conference layout. Figure 3 becomes a multirow arrangement, and v2's combined Figure 4 becomes a separate table and graph. Tables gain benchmark columns and comparator rows, an archival results table and runtime table are added, and retained appendix graphics are resized and relocated.

improvement.justification: V3 addresses an acknowledged error in a central estimator with an explicit factorization and proof, corrected implementation results, and transparent preservation of earlier scores (Appendices B and G). The revised consistency condition, scalability measurements, and clearer applicability boundaries substantially improve technical reliability and evidential support. Its blanket stronger-performance wording exceeds the mixed replacement scores, and the counterfactual table's numerical reassignment remains unexplained, but these reporting limitations do not outweigh the central improvements.
